**The subject changed.** Moritz, 2026-09-25: *"doing the same great job we did for forward also for
backward ... using what already exists in the tenstorrent repositories. adapting. taking inspiration
from gpu implementations ... full speed. with multiple agents."* Correctness is settled and stays
settled. What is open is speed: **58-67x whole step vs whole step at crop 384 (466.70 s against
7-8 s), of which ~8.5x compute / ~11x bandwidth is hardware and ~6-7x is software.** The sprint
wins the software part or says why it cannot. 5x chip-to-chip is below the silicon floor and this
campaign does not promise it.

PROTOCOL: `~/.coworker/state/of3t/PROTOCOL.md`, **forty-six amendments; this field is an INDEX, not
a copy** (it carried ~4 KB of transcribed amendment text until this pass, re-read beside the file
that already holds them). **A46, written THIS pass and before any sprint number exists, is the
rule for the new subject: a backward kernel's win is graded on the VJP, priced against the roof
that binds, and held against inference.** Its six clauses: the VJP against a float64 reference
itself validated by central finite differences, per-tensor worst case located by parameter path,
because a forward check is blind here (a bfp8 arm on this fleet read forward cosine 0.99999 and
backward Inf/NaN); every saving names the roof that binds the part it saves, after 18 passes lost
to a phantom 4.4x from pricing a DRAM-bound op against a dense-cube compute roof; the axis, the
DURING-sampled AICLK and the board class are part of the number; inference is held as a hard stop
with an A/B against an A/A floor on every model that executes a shared site; adapt before you
author and cite what you took; gates are batched and a stack is approved whole. A46 licenses no
speedup that does less of the model's own work. A1-A45 are the correctness protocol and are
unchanged. History: `state/of3t/PASSLOG.md`.

SEQUENCE: **`of3t-bwsurvey`'s JOBS crossed with `of3t-intensity`'s ORDER is the gate on every
kernel row, and it is an AND.** JOBS says what can be built and what tt-train already has; ORDER
says where the seconds actually are. A kernel briefed from one without the other is how a sprint
authors something that saves nothing, and this campaign has burned the ORDER half twice — 18
passes on a phantom 4.4x headroom, and three consecutive wrong conclusions from a "% of peak"
against a roof nobody had established. So: **no kernel row is dispatched this pass, and that is
the correct state, not a stall.** The four rows are 30 minutes old.

`of3t-tapedfwd` is the one that can change the plan rather than feed it. If a taped call still
switches fused triangle attention off for the whole process, then part of the 6-7x is kernels we
already have being bypassed, and that is a wiring fix ahead of any authoring. Its COST number
decides the sprint's order, so I read it before I size anything. It gates nothing formally; it can
shrink what the kernel rows are for.

`of3t-throughput` runs alongside and gates nothing. Its output is the axis correction: chip-to-chip
58-67x is the wrong headline for a box anyone would buy, and samples/sec per box, per dollar and
per watt is the number nobody has computed.

When JOBS and ORDER both land I dispatch the kernel rows from
`perf/of3t_orchestrator/bwd/KERNEL_ROW_TEMPLATE.md` (committed this pass), biggest share of the
6-7x first, each named for its OP and never for OpenFold3 — a backward kernel is engine-level and
serves Boltz-2, OF3T, BC2 and RFD3. The template carries its DONE_CHECK `EXTRA` entry beside the
brief so both halves of the dispatch land together (R193).

GRADIENT-CONFIDENCE: Confident, and verified rather than inferred: OpenFold3's training gradient on Tenstorrent is upstream 0.4.3's gradient to within upstream's own bf16 error, on every section, over the whole step. It rests on the four fields below, each read off its artifact by `perf/of3t_orchestrator/charter/charter_evidence.py` into `state/of3t/CHARTER_EVIDENCE.json` (5 of 5 MET, spec sha `b8874583f28b` equal to this gate's, break control green), on `wk/of3t` `f01fa0813`.

GRADIENTS: Whole-model, every parameter: 4152 tensors of the full training step (trunk, diffusion, distogram, confidence heads), one 384-wide denoise step, scored per tensor by `perf/of3t_fullstep64/score.py` against the A40-validated float64 reference with upstream's own bf16 step as the bar (`perf/of3t_paedraws/SCORE_PD384.json`). 0 unread, 0 placed-but-carried-nothing, 0 multi-placed; global rel 1.55834e-01 against bf16's 9.48232e-01; 98.07 % of the float64 mass at or better than bf16 on draw 0 and 99.13 % on the six-draw mean (A45, `perf/of3t_orchestrator/a45/DRAWS_A45.json`). Worst systematic case: `aux_heads.distogram.linear.weight` at 1.44x its bf16 on every draw (D270, 0.857 % of mass), inside the 3x section bar; all 21 of 21 sections within 3x (`SECTIONS_PD384.json`).

TRAJECTORY: 20 steps, coupled, whole model covering 89.2106 % of its squared gradient norm (`perf/of3t_trajfull/traj_trajfull.json`); upstream's weights move at 19 of 20 steps and ours at all 20. Operating point stated in the artifact: the LR ramp reaches 11.4 % of peak and the clip coefficient is 1.0 throughout, so the knee, the decay and an active clip are driven by the state-free factor checks in PROTOCOL, not by this run.

COVERAGE: All 8 of upstream's LossWeights terms and all 11 conditional paths fire at runtime on the batch, each with the stage and dataset that carried it (`perf/of3t_orchestrator/coverage/COVERAGE_MERGED.json`).
DOESNOT: **This proves the UPDATE RULE over N steps. It does not prove stability over a full
training run**, and no artifact of this campaign may be described as one. Specifically not proven:
behaviour over 100k steps, precision drift accumulating across a long run, rare sample types the
batch never contained, and convergence to upstream's published weights. The honest sentence is
*"our training step is their training step, verified per-parameter with full path coverage"*.

**And the sprint's own bound, stated before its first number exists.** A speed result says seconds
off one crop-384 step on one board at one clock. It says nothing about a long run's throughput
until `of3t-throughput` supplies the samples/sec axis, and a per-step win does not compose into a
time-to-model claim by arithmetic — the host share is real and this campaign already measured a
sibling case where 79.2 % of a round was host work the port never covered, capping every credited
lever at 1.25x. Stack perturbations are strongly sub-additive, so the sprint's levers are approved
as a stack or not at all, never by summing individual readings.

3. **`grad_bias` is unanswered and it is the decisive question.** `sdpa_bw` returns
   `[grad_Q, grad_K, grad_V]` and treats `attn_mask` as a constant, but triangle attention's bias
   is a learned pair projection and its gradient is how signal reaches the pair track at all. It
   may be nearly free from the softmax intermediates the kernel already saves, or it may be the
   sprint's largest single job. `of3t-bwsurvey` sizes it either way.
4. **The taped forward's fused-kernel coverage is unmeasured at runtime.** A code read does not
   answer it; the whole suspicion is that the code says one thing and the taped run does another.
